summary: The main article describes an NHC-catalyzed generation of aryl radicals for arylacylation of styrenes and C(sp3)-H acylation of amides. It includes 4 figures illustrating mechanisms and substrate scopes, and 2 tables detailing optimization and directing group comparisons.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Activation of aryl halides and aryl radical-mediated NHC catalysis. a Oxidative addition of aryl halide to transition metal. TM, transition metal. b Organic electron donor induced aryl radical generation (recent advance). SET, single electron transfer. OED, organic electron donor. c Generation of aryl radical through NHC catalysis (working hypothesis). d Arylacylation of alkene and C(sp 3 ) -H acylation through NHC catalysis (this work). 1,5-HAT, 1,5hydrogen atom transfer.
items.description: This figure compares traditional transition-metal and organic electron donor methods for aryl radical generation with the newly proposed NHC-catalyzed approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions.
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of NHC catalysts and aryl electrophiles for the intramolecular arylacylation reaction.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Substrate scope of radical relay-type arylacylation of styrenes.
items.description: This figure displays the chemical structures and yields for various products formed by the three-component coupling of aldehydes, styrenes, and aryl iodides.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Possible pathways. a Catalytic cycle for arylacylation of alkene. b Catalytic cycle for C(sp 3 ) -H acylation.
items.description: This figure illustrates the proposed catalytic cycles involving the enolate form of the Breslow intermediate and aryl radical generation.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Substrate scope of C(sp 3 ) -H acylation of secondary amides.
items.description: This figure shows the scope of secondary amides and aldehydes used in the C(sp3)-H acylation protocol, including pharmaceutical derivatives.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Mechanistic considerations for C(sp 3 ) -H acylation of secondary amides.
items.description: This table compares different directing groups based on reduction potential, bond dissociation energy, and activation energy for hydrogen abstraction.
